title: Fill the pycnometer without trapping a bubble
instruction: Tilt and rotate the Eisco PH0122B 50 mL pycnometer to release its shoulder bubble, top up under water, then hold it while seating the stopper straight down until capillary overflow. Release both.
context: Laboratory staff remove trapped air before density weighing. Figures obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026): 20–40% of first fills trap about 0.25 mL under the ground joint or shoulder. Recovery uses gentle tilt, rotation and tapping, top-up and straight capillary stoppering. That bubble displaces 0.5% of a 50 mL sample. This water-only instrument trial does not certify an assay.
setup: Eisco PH0122B 50 mL borosilicate 3.3 bottle: 50.8 mm diameter, 69.85 mm bare height and 101.6 mm assembled height, with its native perforated stopper. Dry bottle 40 g, stopper 15 g and seating pressure about 200 g plus a slight twist are figures obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026). The open bottle starts on a shelf with one nominal 0.25 mL shoulder bubble, prepared with a graduated syringe to reproduce the normal first-fill error. The stopper stands freely in a lower-stem guide. Lot A bottle bottom is (180,30,28) mm above the table; B changes y to 75 mm. Stopper tip starts at (270,-150,6) mm and settles to 4 mm. Bath interior is 460×340×90 mm, floor 4 mm and waterline 80 mm. Open seating rest is at (315,30) mm with pad top 6 mm. The reference motion finishes on the existing bath floor at (180,160,4) mm. A 650×650 mm catch area encloses the kit. Sleeved grippers and distal wrists are leak-checked. No fixture clears air or seats the stopper. Inner dimensions, wet friction and fluid rates are estimates. README gives all fixture dimensions, acceptance checks and the USD 330–370 kit allowance.
scoring: After release, support and 1 s stillness with both hands ≥5 mm clear: 0.25 requires shoulder-bubble recovery and ≥45 mL water; 0.50 additionally requires an engaged stopper and ≤1 mL trapped air; 0.75 additionally requires a contact-established seal and ≤0.2 mL air. 1.0 also requires a seat within 2 mm and 10°, ≥0.15 mL counterheld capillary overflow during the final insertion, fresh ≥1.962 N fingertip input and net axial compression near full seating, and dry mass within 0.2 g of the same-pair reference. Untouched start: 0. Broken/lost glass, outside-catch spills, rig damage, bath motion >5 mm/2°, load >40 N or unverifiable history: permanent 0. README defines witnesses and uncertainty.
run_limit: 2400 control steps per trial (120 s at 20 Hz). Reference demo and Dream-1 each cover two trials: A and B.
reset_notes: Use the same stock Eisco PH0122B pair. Fill about one-third up the ground neck as its maker describes, then gently top up down the neck wall. Stage the brim-full open bottle at the lot pose ±1 mm first. Then, for repeatable replication of the observed first-fill error, inject one nominal 0.25 mL air charge with a 1 mL syringe graduated at 0.01 mL and a blunt bent needle under the shoulder on the side facing the robot bases (toward -x; azimuth 180° ±30°, 0° pointing away from the arms), and withdraw the needle without touching the bottle. Accept one shoulder bubble and no separate neck/capillary pockets; no one-degree placement or image-based start-volume estimate. If it splits, reaches the neck or vents, drain and repeat, counting the retry. Shoulder pockets of this size persist at rest in 20–40% of the technician's first fills, so a pinned pocket is the normal state. Stop after five rejected injections, log a failed preparation and do not run the trial. Stage the stopper freely in its 23×23 mm lower-stem guide. Set the bath to 80±1 mm; hands clear and sleeves leak-free. Once per session check the syringe, same-pair capacity, imaging and balance. Under 2 minutes per prepared reset including one retry is an unmeasured planning estimate. Log all attempts and elapsed time. See fixture/RESET-PROTOCOL.md. The phone figures are obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026).
fidelity: Inventory, not CFD. One 0.25 mL shoulder pocket; estimated retention 1.79 mN, mobility 0.025 Ns/m. Tilt vents; bath tops up. Phone figures: 40 g bottle, 15 g stopper, 200 g seating pressure. Native fingertip input and net glass compression each ≥1.962 N; no stopper wrench. Seal proxy 0.2 N; counterhold 1.3/0.3 N per pad. Water mass, COM and inertia; buoyancy/drag caps 1.2/0.6 N. Fit, wetting and flow remain estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: A 0.0, B 0.0 (it did not release the shoulder bubble). Reference demo: A 1.0, B 1.0 (mean 1.0). Both on the same final source and instruction. No hardware result.
